battle.name: 下關戰爭
battle.brief: 一八六三年九月五日起，英、法、美、荷、普、丹六國艦隊兩度炮擊下關海峽，迫使長州藩開港並准許外國人購馬，一八六四年一月十六日更以約二千人的上陸部隊攻佔唐戶、垢田兩座砲台。卡面加特林機槍是一八六〇年取得美國專利的速射武器，參戰的美國正是其本國；海峽裡真正開火的是艦載前膛與後膛砲。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 下關戰爭的交戰方是兩團力量。一團是英國、法國、美國、荷蘭、普魯士與丹麥組成的六國聯合軍隊，另一團是日本長州藩。聯軍不是臨時拼湊的義勇兵，而是各國駐遠東的常備海軍：英國以東印度分隊與中國分隊的蒸汽巡洋艦、蒸汽砲艦為主力，並從印度洋抽調武裝船輸送上陸部隊與糧秣；法國、荷蘭、普魯士各由本國東印度艦隊派出小型巡洋艦與砲艦，參戰人員以海軍水兵與海軍陸戰隊為主，幾乎沒有成建制的陸軍；美國由駐太平洋分隊派一艘軍艦隨英方行動；丹麥方面派出的是駐遠東的小型蒸汽砲艦。六國之間並沒有常設的聯軍司令部，實際的作戰節奏由英方分隊司令掌握，外交交涉則集中於駐日公使一人：英國公使哈里·帕克斯是六國的共同發言人，談判破裂後各艦才依計畫開火。英方分隊的指揮體系是典型的海軍式，旗艦設總部，各艦自行測量與瞄射，參謀只分派射擊目標。長州藩一方則是典型的藩主直轄軍：藩主毛利敬親坐鎮萩城，家老毛利廣信主管外交與軍政，兵員以鄉士與藩士為主，分成海岸隊與山陰隊擔負守備，砲台由法國技師萊昂斯·韋爾尼指導修建。幕府作為下關的直轄宗主並非交戰方，卻在町區留有守備，最後以條約承受了聯軍的全部要求。
countriesEn: There were two sides in the Shimonoseki war. One was a six-power allied fleet made up of Britain, France, the United States, the Netherlands, Prussia and Denmark; the other was the Choshu domain of Japan. The allied force was not a hastily assembled volunteer show but the standing navies of the various powers stationed in the Far East: Britain supplied the main body from its East Indies and China stations in steam corvettes and steam gunboats, and drew armed steamers from the Indian Ocean to carry landing parties and stores; France, the Netherlands and Prussia each sent small cruisers and gunboats from their own East Indies squadrons, their personnel being almost entirely naval ratings and marines, with hardly any formed army units; the United States sent a single warship from its Pacific squadron to act with the British; Denmark contributed the small steam gunboats it kept in the Far East. There was no standing allied command structure: the tempo of the fighting was in the hands of the British station commander, while the diplomacy was concentrated in a single man, the British minister to Japan, Harry Parkes, who spoke for the six. When the negotiations broke down it was his order that set the squadrons on their course. The British command system was the classic naval one, with the flagship serving as headquarters, each ship doing its own ranging and sighting, and the staff distributing targets. The Choshu side was a typical domain army under the direct command of its lord: the lord Mōchi Yoshi(tsugu) sat at Hagi, the chief retainer Mōri Hironobu handled foreign affairs and military administration, and the men were drawn from the local gentry and retainers, divided into coastal units and units for the mountain side of the province; the batteries were built under the direction of the French engineer Léonce Verny. The shogunate, as the sovereign of Shimonoseki as a direct-controlled town, was not a belligerent, but it did keep a garrison in the town and finally bore the whole of the allied demands under the terms of a treaty.
people: 兩邊各有一批人把衝突推到了開火的地步。英國駐日公使哈里·帕克斯最關鍵：他在明治六年到明治八年間駐日，主導條約改正交涉，屢次以書面向幕府要求開放下關、增加通商口岸、准許外國人購買軍馬，判定長州藩不會讓步之後便推動海軍施壓。幕府方面的決策者是征夷大將德川慶喜與老中三條實美；幕府承認下關是直轄地，艦隊的攻擊目標又落在町區，卻既無力阻止也無力反擊，最後只能照單接受條約。長州藩一邊，家老毛利廣信主持外交與密貿易，是藩與英方往來的核心；高杉晉作策劃並指揮奇兵隊，主張以小規模的奇襲對付洋槍與洋艦，桂久武則組建神風隊，以洋式操練和短程突擊彌補火力與裝備的差距。一八六三年五月五日，薩摩的中浦重和與西鄉隆盛在長崎為薩長同盟的密約作中間人，同年底兩藩往來固定；一八六四年一月第二次下關砲擊之後，長州在外交上更形孤立，薩摩與長州的合作從此固定下來，西鄉隆盛與鰐屋一心則在京都一方面籌劃薩長的行動、一方面接觸新政府方面的勢力。坂本龍馬同年在長崎透過商人為長州購得數百支新式步槍；法國技師萊昂斯·韋爾尼則主持修建下關砲台，使長州在硬體上得以抵擋艦砲。
peopleEn: On each side a handful of people drove the conflict to the point of gunfire. The most important was Harry Parkes, the British minister to Japan, who served from 1863 to 1865 and directed the treaty revision negotiations, repeatedly writing to the shogunate to demand that Shimonoseki be opened, that the number of treaty ports be increased and that foreigners be allowed to buy horses; having concluded that the Choshu domain would not give way, he pushed for naval pressure. On the shogunate side the decision makers were the shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu and the senior councilor Sanjo Sanetomi; the shogunate accepted that Shimonoseki was direct-controlled territory and the targets of the squadron lay inside the town, yet it was neither able to prevent nor to answer the attack, and could only accept the terms as they were presented. On the Choshu side the chief retainer Mōri Hironobu handled foreign affairs and the illicit trade and was the core of the domain's dealings with the British; Takasugi Shinsaku planned and commanded the kibintai, arguing that small irregular raids were the answer to foreign rifles and foreign warships, while his brother Takasugi Kikusu formed the shimpūtai, training men in Western drill and short rushes to make up for the deficit in firepower and equipment. On 5 May 1863 Nakaura Shigekazu of Satsuma and Saigo Takamori acted as intermediaries at Nagasaki for the secret agreement of the Satsuma-Choshu alliance, and by the end of that year relations between the two domains were regular; after the second bombardment of Shimonoseki in January 1864 the diplomatic isolation of Choshu grew worse, the Satsuma-Choshu cooperation was thereby fixed, and Saigo Takamori and Ichi Takamiya worked in Kyoto both to plan the movements of the Satsuma-Choshu side and to make contact with the forces around the new government. In the same year Sakamoto Ryoma bought several hundred modern rifles for Choshu through merchants at Nagasaki; the French engineer Léonce Verny directed the building of the Shimonoseki batteries, which gave Choshu the means to hold out against naval gunfire.
kits: 卡面這件加特林機槍本身並沒有出現在下關海峽，但它屬於同一個技術世代，可以放在正確的位置上看。理查德·喬登·加特林在一八六零年取得美國專利，初型為六根槍管、以手搖曲柄帶動、槍身連架重約三百磅，理論射速可達每分鐘數百發；優點是後坐力分散在六次擊發上，弱點是全靠人力轉動，連續射擊之後槍管很快發熱，射速便要下降。一八六一年南北戰爭爆發後，聯邦軍率先裝備這種武器，第一次馬納薩斯之役中因操作生疏未能發揮作用，到一八六二年的沙伊洛與安提塔姆之役才見到它的價值；一八六四年美國陸軍把它列為制式武器，南方軍政府也購買並繳獲了一批，一八六四年九月亞特蘭大陷落時落入南方手中的十數挺，後來在維吉尼亞一線被使用。下關方面，聯軍參戰的艦隻裝備的是前膛滑膛砲與線膛後膛砲一類的艦砲，英國主力艦多備有阿姆斯特朗式線膛後膛砲與達格倫式前膛滑膛砲，砲彈從艦側直接打向岸上砲台；上陸部隊帶的是撞擊式（percussion）步槍，英軍為一八五三年式與一八五五年式恩菲爾德步槍，法軍為一八五七年式與一八六一年式步槍，並配有騎槍與輕型野砲。長州藩這邊，下關砲台架的是十九世紀中期的前膛滑膛大砲，射程不算遠，卻占著海峽兩岸的險要位置；藩兵除了原有的火繩與燧發舊槍，還從密貿易管道取得撞擊式步槍、鉛彈與火藥。破壞器材方面，長州一方曾用大量火藥製成的爆炸物去炸襲居留地，聯軍一方則靠艦砲的爆炸彈與登陸部隊的突襲。
kitsEn: The Gatling gun on this card never appeared in the Shimonoseki strait, but it belongs to the same technological generation and can be placed in the right position. Richard Jordan Gatling took out a United States patent in 1860; the first model had six barrels, was turned by a hand crank, and weighed about three hundred pounds with its mount, giving a theoretical rate of fire of several hundred rounds a minute. Its strength was that the recoil was spread over six separate discharges; its weakness was that it turned entirely on human muscle, and once firing was sustained the barrels heated quickly and the rate fell away. When the American Civil War broke out in 1861 the Union army equipped with the weapon first; it was of little use at the first battle of Manassas because the crews were untrained, and only at Shiloh and Antietam in 1862 did it show its worth. In 1864 the United States army made it a standard arm, and the Confederate states bought quantities and captured more; a dozen or more that fell into Southern hands when Atlanta fell in September 1864 were later used in Virginia. On the Shimonoseki side the allied ships carried naval guns of the smoothbore muzzle-loading and rifled breech-loading types, British capital ships carrying both Armstrong rifled breech-loaders and Dahlgren smoothbore muzzle-loaders, firing their shells straight from the broadside onto the shore batteries. The landing parties carried percussion rifles: the British Pattern 1853 and Pattern 1855 Enfields, the French the modèle 1857 and modèle 1861 rifles, together with bayonets and light field pieces. On the Chōshū side the Shimonoseki batteries mounted mid-nineteenth century smoothbore muzzle-loading guns, not long-ranged, but holding the commanding ground on both shores of the strait; besides their old matchlock and flintlock pieces the retainers obtained percussion rifles, lead and powder through the channels of the illicit trade. As for matériel for destruction, the Chōshū side used charges of packed gunpowder to blow up the foreign settlement, while the allies relied on the explosive shells of their naval guns and on the shock of the landing parties.
tactics: 第一次下關砲擊是報復式的：談判破裂後，聯軍艦隊駛入下關海峽，遭到岸上長州砲台射擊，隨即以艦砲還擊數小時，把數門砲打成啞砲、守備隊退回堡壘內而結束。第二次完全不同：一八六四年一月十六日，艦隊在更能俯瞰砲台的位置集中艦砲火力，先以長時間的連續射擊壓制砲台指揮，再在十七日由登陸部隊在垢田與唐戶兩處灘頭上岸，占領並破壞砲台，舉旗示範佔領後才退泊他處。關門海峽的潮流在滿潮時急得驚人，蒸汽帆船必須由汽艇曳航才能通過，加上是一月的北風季節，艦隊的機動與射擊精度都受限制，這也是登陸作戰被排在第二天白天進行的原因之一。長州方面的戰術是守點與襲擊並行：下關砲台採法式環形土壘，射界交叉、彈藥庫設在土堤之下、守備分層配置，一旦艦火壓制便由夜襲小隊遷出；奇兵隊在同年二月十三日企圖用爆炸物襲擊神奈川的外国人居留地，事敗後首謀者多人被處決，神風隊則以洋式操練準備短程的白刃突擊。嚴罰之後，長州把正規作戰轉向分散的游擊，一八六六年第二次長州征討時由游擊隊在山間與內陸作持久抵抗。補給方面，聯軍的糧秣與彈藥自母港與印度洋基地運來，藩兵則靠密貿易得來的火藥與鉛彈維持，冷兵器與舊式火繩槍仍在鄉士手中使用。
tacticsEn: The first bombardment of Shimonoseki was retaliatory: once the negotiations broke down the allied squadrons drove into the strait, were fired on by the Chōshū shore batteries, and returned the fire with their naval guns for several hours, silencing several of the batteries and driving the garrison back into the works before the squadrons withdrew. The second was quite different: on 16 January 1864 the fleet concentrated its naval gunfire from positions that overlooked the batteries, using long periods of continuous fire to suppress the battery commanders, and on the seventeenth the landing parties went ashore at the beaches of Arita and Karato, occupied and destroyed the batteries, raised flags to make the occupation plain, and only then stood off to another anchorage. The tide in the Kanmon strait runs hard at the flood, and steam sailing ships had to be towed through by steam launches; the season was the north wind of January as well, and the manoeuvring and the accuracy of the allied fire were both limited, which was one reason the landing was set for the second day in daylight. The Chōshū side combined the defence of fixed points with sudden attack: the Shimonoseki batteries were built in French style with a ring earthwork, intersecting fields of fire, ammunition magazines dug under the ramparts and a garrison posted in tiers, and once the naval fire weighed on them small night parties withdrew from the positions. In the same year, on 13 February, the kibintai attempted to blow up the foreign settlement at Kanagawa with a charge of explosives, and after the attempt failed several of the leaders were executed; the shimpūtai meanwhile trained in Western drill in preparation for short rushes with the bayonet. After the punishment the domain turned its regular warfare into dispersed guerrilla action, and in the second Chōshū expedition of 1866 partisan units fought a prolonged resistance in the mountains and the interior. On supply, the allies drew their food and ammunition from their home stations and from bases in the Indian Ocean, while the domain's men were kept going by powder and lead bought through the illicit trade, with cold weapons and old matchlocks still in the hands of the local gentry.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。一八六三年八月，長州藩的浪人拿捕美國商船 George C. Muskogee，傷及船員，生麥事件成為聯軍追究的近因。一八六三年九月五日，第一次下關砲擊爆發，六國艦隊以十數艘的規模在海峽內炮擊，長州數門砲台失去作戰能力，町區遭到牽連。一八六四年一月十六日與十七日，第二次下關砲擊，艦隊規模較前次增加，上陸部隊約二千人，垢田與唐戶兩座砲台被占領並破壞。一八六四年六月，長州藩的軍隊占領了幕府在長府的支廳與代官所，長府占領事件成為幕府追究藩的直接理由；同年秋，幕府對長州藩課以嚴罰，藩主被幽禁，家老被罷免，在江戶的交涉負責人被拘禁。一八六四年九月六日，與英、法、荷、普魯士、美國五國簽訂下關條約，開放下關、箱館與新潟三港，外國人可以在下關購買軍馬，並得派駐領事。人員損失方面，雙方都沒有留下可靠的官方統計，通行說法是數十人規模，多是砲火與登陸作戰中的傷者。卡面武器方面，加特林機槍一八六〇年取得專利，初型六管、重約三百磅，一八六四年成為美國陸軍制式武器。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. In August 1863 the Chōshū irregulars seized the American merchantman George C. Muskogee and injured her crew; the Namago incident became the immediate pretext on which the allies pressed their complaints. On 5 September 1863 the first bombardment of Shimonoseki was opened, the six navies engaging inside the strait with a force of a dozen or more ships, and several Chōshū batteries were put out of action, with the town itself affected. On 16 and 17 January 1864 came the second bombardment, with a larger concentration of shipping than the first time and a landing force of about two thousand men, which occupied and destroyed the batteries at Arita and Karato. In June 1864 Chōshū troops occupied the shogunate's sub-office and deputy magistrate's office at Nagafu; the Nagafu occupation became the direct reason for the shogunate to call the domain to account. In the autumn of the same year the shogunate imposed a severe punishment on Chōshū: the lord was placed under house arrest, the chief retainer was dismissed, and the man who had conducted the negotiations in Edo was detained. On 6 September 1864 the Convention of Shimonoseki was signed with Britain, France, the Netherlands, Prussia and the United States, opening the three ports of Shimonoseki, Hakodate and Niigata, allowing foreigners to buy horses at Shimonoseki, and providing for the stationing of consuls. On losses, neither side left reliable official figures; the usual account is a scale of some dozens of men, mostly casualties of the bombardment and of the landing operations. As for the weapon on the card, the Gatling gun was patented in 1860, the first model having six barrels and weighing about three hundred pounds, and it became a standard weapon of the United States army in 1864.
cause: 起因是修約交涉的全面停滯。幕府在一八五八年簽訂的通商條約只開放橫濱、新潟與長崎，此後列強要求重訂條約、擴大通商口岸並取得內國航行的權利，條約改正交涉從一八六〇年起拖了三年而無結果；其中卡得最死的一條，就是下關的開港與軍馬的買賣——外國人想在長州藩的核心地帶取得據點並採買軍用馬匹，長州藩以既有的禁止武器輸出與限制外國人貿易的方針一口回絕。層層壓力之下，幕府在處理對外事務上的無力也暴露無遺：生麥事件中藩屬拿捕美國船並傷及船員，使聯軍懷疑長州藩的武裝並非出於個別分子的衝動，而是有計劃地挑戰條約體制；同時修約中最棘手的一條，是日本方面承諾限制本國向外國輸出武器與船隻，而長州藩仍透過密貿易繼續購買洋槍，幕府無法制止。結果談判桌上談不成的條件，全部轉成了海峽裡的砲火。
causeEn: The cause was the complete breakdown of the treaty revision negotiations. The commercial treaties the shogunate signed in 1858 had opened only Yokohama, Niigata and Nagasaki, and afterwards the Western powers demanded a revision, an enlargement of the number of treaty ports, and rights of inland navigation; the revision talks, begun in 1860, dragged on for three years without result. The hardest condition of all was the opening of Shimonoseki and the sale of horses: the foreign powers wanted a foothold in the very heart of the Chōshū domain and wished to buy war horses, and the domain refused in a single stroke, holding to its established policy of prohibiting the export of weapons and restricting foreign trade. Under the accumulating pressure the shogunate's helplessness in foreign affairs was laid bare: in the Namago incident domain men seized an American ship and injured her crew, and the allies came to suspect that Chōshū's armed men were not acting on the impulse of individual hotheads but were deliberately challenging the treaty system; at the same time the most awkward clause of the revision was Japan's promise to restrict the export of weapons and shipping to foreigners, while the Chōshū continued to buy foreign rifles through the illicit trade and the shogunate could not stop it. The result was that every condition that could not be settled at the negotiating table turned into gunfire in the strait.
impact: 後果是多重的。第一，條約把幕府逼到了開國的最後一級台階：下關條約是幕府與列強之間最後一份不平等條約，開港、購馬與領事制度把主權的讓渡具體化，也讓尊王攘夷一派對幕府的怨恨達到頂點；同年秋的嚴罰與一八六六年的第二次長州征討之後，這份怨恨在幕內迅速轉化為倒幕的行動力。第二，長州藩被迫接受在他們自己的家門內開港，等於讓列強在長州的核心地帶立起了法權，門戶被打開之後，薩摩與長州都明白單靠一藩之力無法與列強周旋，薩長同盟與後來的倒幕軍政府因此更快成形。第三，軍事上這兩次砲擊把西洋艦砲與岸壁砲台之間的差距公開演示了一遍：長州此後在軍備上轉向彈藥自給與游擊作戰，幕府則加快購買線膛後膛砲並整飭海防，日本近代海軍與炮兵制度的骨架都沿著這段經驗往前走。第四，港口本身的命運被改變：下關自此成為通商口岸，後來與箱館、新潟一起經歷明治時期的開港波動，直到今日仍是本州與九州之間的門戶與主要港口。
impactEn: The consequences were multiple. First, the treaty pushed the shogunate to the last rung of the ladder of opening: the Convention of Shimonoseki was the last unequal treaty signed by the shogunate with the Western powers, and the opening of the port, the purchase of horses and the institution of consulates gave a concrete form to the surrender of sovereignty, while at the same time it drove the resentment of the sonno joiyi party against the shogunate to its height. After the severe punishment of the autumn of 1864 and the second Chōshū expedition of 1866 that resentment was converted inside the shogunate's own camp into the driving force of the movement to overthrow it. Second, the Chōshū domain was made to accept the opening of a port within its own territory, which amounted to letting the Western powers set up their law in the middle of Chōshū; once that door stood open, both Satsuma and Chōshū understood that a single domain could not stand against the foreign powers, and the Satsuma-Chōshū alliance and the government that later overthrew the shogunate took shape all the faster. Third, militarily, the two bombardments demonstrated in public the gap between Western naval guns and shore batteries: from then on Chōshū turned in the military field towards self-supplied ammunition and guerrilla warfare, while the shogunate hastened to buy rifled breech-loading guns and to reform its coastal defence, and the skeleton of the modern Japanese navy and artillery system grew out of that experience. Fourth, the fate of the port itself was changed: Shimonoseki became a treaty port, and later, together with Hakodate and Niigata, went through the fluctuations of the opening in the Meiji period, remaining to this day the gateway and principal port between Honshu and Kyushu.
result: 結果是長州在砲火中失敗，在條約上讓步。下關砲台在第二次砲擊之後失守，長州藩守備隊退往內陸；一八六四年九月六日，幕府以自己的名義與英、法、荷、普魯士、美國簽訂下關條約，開放下關、箱館、新潟三港並准許外國人購買軍馬，聯軍這才從海峽撤出。就在同一年的六月與秋天，長州藩先後爆發長府占領事件並被幕府課以嚴罰，藩主受幽禁、家老被罷免，藩勢大衰，藩內強硬派因此加速投向倒幕一途。一八六六年幕府發動第二次長州征討，長州方面在山陰被各路軍分割殲滅，藩主與家老事後皆被幕府收押或免職，殘部則轉入山間作游擊抵抗，翌年由新政府另行處置藩主與藩政。開港本身並未因戰爭結束而固定：新政府於一八六六年表明要重訂開港條約，箱館與新潟的開港又因一八六八至一八六九年的箱館事件而一度停止，數年後才重新開放；下關則一直是日本海上的固定門戶，也是海峽航線的兩端各一次重建秩序的地方。
resultEn: The result was that Chōshū was defeated by gunfire and gave way in the treaty. The batteries at Shimonoseki were lost after the second bombardment and the Chōshū garrison withdrew inland; on 6 September 1864 the shogunate, in its own name, signed the Convention of Shimonoseki with Britain, France, the Netherlands, Prussia and the United States, opening the three ports of Shimonoseki, Hakodate and Niigata and permitting foreigners to buy horses, and only then did the allied force withdraw from the strait. In that same year, in June and in the autumn, Chōshū was involved first in the occupation of Nagafu and then in the severe punishment meted out by the shogunate: the lord was put under house arrest, the chief retainer was dismissed, the power of the domain declined sharply, and the hard line inside the domain was thereby driven all the faster towards the movement to overthrow the shogunate. In 1866 the shogunate launched the second Chōshū expedition, the Chōshū forces were cut up and destroyed piecemeal in the mountain side of the province, the lord and the chief retainer were afterwards all seized by the shogunate or removed from office, and the remnants turned to guerrilla resistance in the hills, the lord and the domain government being dealt with separately by the new government in the following year. The opening itself did not become fixed by the end of the war: the new government declared in 1866 that the port-opening treaties were to be revised, and the opening of Hakodate and Niigata was suspended for a time as a result of the Hakodate incident of 1868 and 1869, to be resumed some years later; Shimonoseki, meanwhile, remained the fixed gateway to the Sea of Japan, and the place where the order of the strait was rebuilt once more.
